subject: Pilot invite: Optimize Quality Guardrails (gating) for Acme Fintech
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmefintech.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 2, 2024 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Pilot invite: Optimize Quality Guardrails (gating) for Acme Fintech

Hi Maya,

Following up on last week’s conversation about the quantization-related quality dip you saw during your last round of cost tuning.

We’re launching a design-partner pilot for a new capability in Redwood Optimize: **Quality Guardrails (gating)**. The idea is simple: when Optimize proposes a cost-saving config change (e.g., quant profile transition, batching/caching knobs, routing tweaks), Redwood runs a targeted eval suite and only allows the change to be applied if quality stays within agreed thresholds.

I’d love to invite Acme Fintech to be part of the pilot. What we’re looking for:

1) **A prompt set / eval inputs** representative of your production traffic (sanitized is fine). We can start small.
2) **One or two key routes/models** where Optimize is currently active or you’re considering enabling it.
3) 1–2 technical points of contact to join a kickoff and help us validate pass/fail outcomes.

What you’ll get:
- “Observe-only” mode first (no blocking): you’ll see pass/fail + metric deltas before any enforcement.
- Option to move to “soft-block” (override available with audit trail), then “hard-block” once you’re comfortable.
- A summary of learnings + recommended thresholds for your workload.

Proposed timeline:
- **Week of Dec 9**: 45-min kickoff + prompt set ingestion
- **Week of Dec 16**: run initial evals against your current baseline + 1–2 Optimize proposals
- **Early Jan**: enable gating in observe-only on your tenant; iterate if we see false positives/negatives

Prompt set request (initial version):
- 100–300 examples (more is great, but not required)
- Include any strict formatting requirements (JSON schema, tool-calling, compliance wording)
- For each example: input prompt + any system instructions + expected rubric/constraints (if you have them)

Security note: you can fully redact customer identifiers and account numbers. If you prefer not to share prompts, we can instead run a joint session where you provide a smaller synthetic set + we help you build coverage from there.

Attaching:
- Redwood_Optimize_Guardrails_Pilot_Overview.pdf
- Prompt_Set_Template_v1.csv

Would you be open to joining the pilot? If yes, can you share who should be on the kickoff from your side, and what days/times are easiest next week?

Thanks,
Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Optimize
Redwood Inference



From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmefintech.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Dec 2, 2024 at 1:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot invite: Optimize Quality Guardrails (gating) for Acme Fintech

Hi Aditya,

Yes, we’re interested. This is exactly the type of safety net we were asking for.

A few questions before we commit:
1) Where do the prompts live (your infra vs ours)? We have constraints around leaving our environment.
2) Who at Redwood can access the prompt set, and how long do you retain it?
3) For an override, can we require a second approval / audit log export?

I can bring Daniel (ML Eng lead) and one of our platform engineers to a kickoff. Next week: Tue 2–4pm PT or Thu 10–11:30am PT.

Thanks,
Maya

Maya Patel
Director of ML Platform
Acme Fintech



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmefintech.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 3, 2024 at 9:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot invite: Optimize Quality Guardrails (gating) for Acme Fintech

Hi Maya,

Great — and all good questions.

1) **Where prompts live**
For the pilot, we support two options:
- **Redwood-hosted eval runner** (fastest to start): you upload a sanitized prompt set to a restricted folder; we run eval jobs in our infra.
- **Customer-hosted prompt storage**: we can reference prompts from a location you control (e.g., your S3/GCS) via short-lived credentials. This takes a bit longer to wire up but keeps content in your environment.

2) **Access + retention**
Access is limited to the Applied ML/Evals on-call group and the pilot engineering team as needed for debugging gating outcomes (we can keep this to a small named list). We store:
- the prompt content (if you choose Redwood-hosted) and
- derived eval artifacts (scores, aggregated metrics, deltas)

For pilot defaults, we’re proposing **30 days retention** for raw prompts, and longer retention for aggregated metrics/audit summaries. If you need a shorter window, we can accommodate.

3) **Override controls + audit export**
Overrides are restricted (RBAC) and captured in an audit event with: who requested, who approved, justification, eval run id, and which thresholds were bypassed.

For “second approval”: we can support a policy of “override requires approver role” (separate from requestor). If you want a true two-person rule, we can align that during kickoff.

Audit export: we can provide JSON exports and can discuss your SIEM needs.

Scheduling: Thu 10–11am PT works on my end (could do 60 minutes). If you confirm, Miguel will send a calendar invite.

Also, if helpful: you can start with a small prompt subset (~100) focused on the route where you saw the quantization regression, then expand coverage.

Best,
Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Optimize
Redwood Inference



From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@acmefintech.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmefintech.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 3, 2024 at 3:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot invite: Optimize Quality Guardrails (gating) for Acme Fintech

Hi Aditya,

Jumping in — I’m Daniel (ML Eng lead).

Two technical clarifications:
- Are you measuring “quality” only via rubric/LLM-judge style metrics, or can we include strict checks (e.g., JSON validity, schema conformance, tool call shape)?
- For quantization specifically, do you recommend different suites depending on model family? Our main route is chat w/ structured JSON output.

We can bring a sanitized set. We also have a small internal harness that checks JSON schema + a couple of “no hallucinated fields” rules.

Thu 10am PT works.

Thanks,
Daniel



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@acmefintech.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmefintech.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.santos@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 4, 2024 at 4:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot invite: Optimize Quality Guardrails (gating) for Acme Fintech

Hi Daniel,

Yes on both points.

- We support **hard/strict checks** (JSON parseability, schema conformance, presence/absence of required fields, tool call envelope validation) alongside rubric-style metrics. For structured output routes, strict checks are usually the first gate.

- For **quantization**, we do vary suites by **model family + workload tags** (chat vs tool-calling vs structured output). Quant changes can introduce formatting drift and subtle reasoning degradation, so we typically run:
  - a formatting/structure suite (strict)
  - a task success suite (rubric)
  - a small “sensitive cases” suite if the customer has known failure modes

If you have existing JSON/schema checks, we can integrate them as additional validators (either as part of your prompt set metadata or as a custom check step).

Miguel will send the invite for Thu 10am PT shortly. If you want to upload the initial prompt set beforehand, here’s the secure folder link we discussed (access restricted to this pilot):
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mQmPILOT-ACME-REDACTED

See you Thursday.

Best,
Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product, Optimize
Redwood Inference
